correctness.rationale: Realized EF1 is equivalent to the range-at-most-one event for independent bundle success counts. One-trial transfer is coupled as U+Z versus V+Z, with U~Bin(a,p), V~Bin(b-1,p), and Z~Bern(p). The difference is p E[K(U+1,V,C)-K(U,V+1,C)]. Antisymmetry of the bracket, monotonicity for U<V, and the binomial monotone-likelihood-ratio comparison make this nonnegative. The (U,V)=(0,1), all-other-counts-zero contribution supplies the explicit lower bound (b-a-1)p^2(1-p)^(m-2)>0. Finite transfers converge to the balanced size vector and strictness proves uniqueness. Inclusion-exclusion for adjacent count intervals proves the exact formula; the standard binomial local CLT and Gaussian integration give the coefficient (2^n-1)/sqrt(n). Exact testing from verify.py: 7,920 formula/count+optimality tests, 1,458 independent bit-pattern tests, 30,240 strict transfer tests. The infinite claims are proved analytically; numeric checks are not substitutes.

originality.rationale: Closest primary article arXiv:2610.34906v1 treats ex-post exact EF; Section 7.1 and Proposition 7.2 establish equal-realized-value optimality for exact EF and Section 8 explicitly leaves EF1 as a future direction. Its Appendix A.2 provides a general monotone-likelihood-ratio ingredient, but not the claimed EF1 probability optimizer, strict gap, or asymptotic. Other inspected stochastic/online fair division works use different probability spaces or optimize expected envy. Searched aliases included binomial-range Schur concavity and near-equality probability; no direct equivalent or dominating statement was found in accessible records. Unindexed probabilistic majorization literature remains a material priority risk.
residual_risks: A general unindexed majorization theorem for independent binomial ranges might imply the pair-smoothing conclusion.
AAMAS 2024 related full text was not inspected; the accessible abstract concerns a different expected-value objective.
Only iid shared Bernoulli value realizations are covered; extending to heterogeneous or agent-specific valuation lotteries is unresolved.

value.rationale: The 2026 lottery-goods paper specifically leaves EF1 as a natural research direction. An ex-ante fair assignment is not generally safe ex post; here a complete all-n, all-m optimizer classification is proved for the canonical common Bernoulli-valued domain, with a strict quantitative transfer inequality, a closed-form optimal EF1 probability, and the exact polynomial decay rate. This is a motivated natural exact invariant, not an arbitrary fixed table or a trivial relabeling. Under three agents, six goods, p=1/2, balanced gives 23/32 versus 9/16 for sizes (1,2,3). Mathematical significance is restricted to the stated stochastic domain.
